Can’t help but grin looking at this track-spec first-gen Toyota Tacoma . Not pictured is the engine mounted out back in the bed, below the massive rear wing. – Carter Fry

No, you’re not looking at some AI hallucination of a Lexus pickup that doesn’t exist. This is the Meso Customs TX1, a legitimate Lexus pickup based on the Toyota Tacoma and built by the crew at Meso Customs. The front end takes on the look of a Lexus GX , and even the interior gets overhauled to look and feel like what you’d get from the luxury brand. – Jack Fitzgerald

There are plenty of ways to get your race car to the track, but most of them involve purpose-built haulers based on proven HD trucks. Builder Raymond Canales looked at the available options and said, “I can do better.” Then he set to work creating this tag-axle VW hauler based on the beloved Type 2, giving new meaning to its “Transporter” surname. Built specifically to transport his VW Beetle race car, the Type 2 Hauler is just the kind of inspired lunacy with a practical purpose that we can get behind. – Andrew Wendler

Mark Denlinger’s Mad Customs is responsible for this Chevy wagon build. While Nomads get most of the love, this 210 four-door wagon restomod features a natural patina to complement its subtle hardware updates. Yes, it’s lowered, but so deftly it almost appears to just be sitting on a worn suspension; the Forgeline EO1 wheels are painted black to keep a low profile; keep the hood closed, and you’d never see its LT4 GM V-8. Denlinger also fabbed up custom tubs to clear the rear tires and modified the cargo floor to clear the custom exhaust that was crafted in-house. With apologies to Michael Jackson, this is one smooth criminal—if you know where to look. – Andrew Wendler

Steve Stroppe has a history of clean builds, and this Z/28 does nothing to sully that legacy. Featuring a carbureted Chevy big-block and a massaged turbo-hydromantic 400 transmission with a Gear Vendors overdrive, it pays respect to builds of the past. But the craftsmanship is so meticulous, and the Ice Gray Metallic paint and Graphite Blue interior are so sublime, the whole thing makes a contemporary statement without trying too hard. The Camaro was basically the poster child for custom builds in the ‘80s and ‘90s, but for those of us raised in the Rust Belt, there’s still something special about a well-executed 1969 Z/28 project. – Andrew Wendler

(This is one of our best glimpses yet into how many Celestiqs have been sold.) According to the NHTSA recall report , GM is aware of 20 minor accidents due to the fault, two of which resulted in minor injuries. Fortunately, the condition only arises at low speeds, but any loss of braking is a deeply concerning and dangerous occurrence. Two-wheel-drive Cadillac Lyriqs are not included in the recall, and the only Blazer EV trims involved are SS and Police Pursuit Vehicles.

Cadillac Lyriqs are hit hardest by the recall, which includes 474 2023 Lyriqs, 22,819 2024 Lyriqs, 11,926 2025 Lyriqs, 9,322 2026 Lyriqs, and 44 2027 Lyriqs. The recall also includes 13,627 2026 Vistiqs and 5,175 2027 Vistiqs, as well as 51 2025 Celestiqs, and 31 2026 Celestiqs. (This is one of our best glimpses yet into how many Celestiqs have been sold.) The only Chevrolets included in the recall are 562 2024 Blazer EVs, 2012 2025 Blazer EVs, 1,314 2026 Blazer EVs, and 23 2027 Blazer EVs. VINs are already searchable on NHTSA's website , and the remedy comes in the form of an over-the-air update for owners who have opted in to those, otherwise owners will have to take their vehicles to dealerships to have the software update downloaded.

The conditions that lead to the temporary loss of brake function are very specific. According to the recall report and GM's testing, "when the brakes are lightly applied at low speeds during a sharp turn and the vehicle encounters a bump or depression – such as at the end of a driveway – a momentary release and reapplication of the brakes may cause the software's slip calculation to misinterpret wheel movement. In some instances, this may result in a temporary loss of braking. The phenomenon is unique to certain vehicles equipped with performance all-wheel drive (pAWD, RPO X0E) and is resolved when the brakes are applied again."

GM already recalled 21,469 all-wheel-drive Lyriqs for a similar issue in 2024 , but it found that vehicles built with the software changes following that recall and vehicles that already received the software update from that recall are still susceptible to the conditions described in the new recall, and they need the latest update. The latest software update corrects the slip calculation in the vehicle's brake system control module that causes the temporary loss of braking, which coincidentally is the same claim made on the 2024 recall. Hopefully this time it actually fixes the problem.

If you drive one of the cars included in the recall, be aware of the possibility of braking loss, and remember that if you experience braking loss, normal brake function should return on the next brake press. Dealers should already be notified of the recall, but owner notification is estimated to begin on December 14.

title: Stacking Super Duty Trucks And A Lamborghini Huracan STO Is The Ultimate SEMA Flex

article_paragraphs: Oh, that's just $1 million worth of vehicles driving up those ramps

SEMA is one of the few places where a Lamborghini can struggle to stand out. Park one next to a row of wildly modified trucks, and it might barely earn a second glance. Elevation Off Grid (EOG) had a different idea, and frankly, it leverages the Lamborghini in question as more of a prop since the company is really selling the Super Duty trucks it's sitting on. So yeah, this is a sincerely impressive display for multiple reasons.

First, let's break this down a touch. Elevation Off Grid is known for building custom heavy-duty trucks that don't sacrifice their heavy-duty capabilities. EOG created a similar display at SEMA in the past, but with the Lamborghini thrown in the mix, the company estimates there's close to a $1 million elevated 11 feet off the Las Vegas Convention Center floor. Watching the setup of this display is what caught our eye in the first place. Some companies may have used some type of crane or forklift, but once the Lamborghini was loaded onto the Super Duty, ramps were used to drive the car-hauling rig atop the other two shot trucks. We can only imagine that a very confident — and well-insured — driver was piloting that white Ford Super Duty .

Sure, the stunt is cool, and again, it'll get the brand noticed, but there's a somewhat sad detail why this SEMA display caught our eye in the first place. For all the cool stuff we see at SEMA each year, plenty of the cars, trucks, and SUVs in question are little more than fancy rollers. Some don't even have complete powertrains, while others are running Bluetooth driveshafts. While they might look cool, they're often held together with hopes and dreams, and the flashier vehicles tend to be vaporware cars that you could only wish to life .

That's a big reason why this demo from EOG is so cool. Any company can talk a big game, but some actually back their products up. Very few can build a truck that shows off so many concurrent skills in one relatively simple-looking display. Driving a pickup onto ramps is ordinarily unremarkable. Doing it with a Lamborghini behind the cab and two other trucks waiting underneath adds a little more pressure to the job. This all could've been viral for a very different reason.

Then consider what the other two trucks are doing — they're supporting the weight of a custom Super Duty and a Lamborghini. Yes, they're sharing the load, but we're still talking about several thousand pounds on each pickup. The company boasts that its beds are capable of supporting 10,000 pounds (4,536 kg), so in theory, each is doing relatively light work. EOG then uses LiquidSpring Smart Suspension components to keep either truck from squatting under the load. It's a very clever way to make a very clear point.

title: BMW Just Went 186 MPH In The New Alpina 7 Series
raw_summary: Thanks to spy shots, we already knew BMW was hard at work cooking up the next Alpina B7 and that it'll have a V8 that sounds pretty great . The brand has now come out with official footage of the car doing high-speed testing at the Nardò test track, exceeding 186 mph. What, did you think the special label version of BMW's flagship sedan would be slow? For reference, the last-gen Alpina B7 already had a top speed of 205 mph, so 186 was frankly table stakes. That said, the speed itself arguably isn't what BMW is flexing her — it's the peace with which that speed is achieved. "Speed has always been baked into the Alpina brand's DNA," said BMW Alpina vice president Oliver Viellechner. "However, we are not just interested in top speed alone. What matters is how natural, stable and confident it feels to drive at that speed." Internally, the brand apparently calls these cars "distance-shrinking" machines; autobahn weapons made to cover literal continents in great speed, style, and serenity.

Internally, the brand apparently calls these cars "distance-shrinking" machines; autobahn weapons made to cover literal continents in great speed, style, and serenity.

You might recognize the name Nardò, by the way, from "Nardo Gray," that primer-like paint color popularized by Audi. The Nardò Ring, a 7.8-mile test track in southern Italy owned by Porsche and shaped like a perfect circle, is where that comes from.

Other confirmed details now include Alpina-signature 20-spoke lightweight wheels (peeping at the sidewall shows a diameter of 22 inches) wearing specially made tires that feature an extra layer of foam inside allowing for peak high-speed stability and comfort. Four oval exhaust tips emit a "rich, deep sound," and BMW says max torque out of that V8 is available "across virtually the entire rev range," while engine management software and throttle mapping is tweaked for smoothness over aggression. Gearbox tuning, too, has been revised to accommodate the bump in horsepower and engine speeds.

This new B7 (or whatever BMW will choose to call the next Alpina-ized 7 Series) will be the first production car made under the joint BMW Alpina brand. BMW announced that it had acquired Alpina back in 2022, but didn't take full control over the tuner until the beginning of this year. The new BMW Alpina 7 Series will be unveiled next year.

article_paragraphs: Range Rover is pulling the plug on its two most affordable models, the Evoque and Velar, as a new entry-level EV steps in.
For decades, the Range Rover name was viewed as a status symbol, mostly used by wealthy buyers, high-powered executives, and even royalty.
That started to change with the launch of the Evoque in 2011 and the Velar in 2017, making the iconic British luxury brand a little more accessible.

In the US, the 2026 Range Rover Evoque starts at $49,900, and the Velar starts at $61,600. That’s considerably less than the Sport and flagship Range Rover SUVs, which start at $83,700 and $107,400, respectively.

Range Rover’s accessible luxury era is reportedly drawing to a close. Martin Limbert, Range Rover’s managing director, confirmed to Autocar that the Evoque and Velar will officially be discontinued, with production set to end in 2027.
While it has no direct replacement planned, the new Range Rover GT will serve as the brand’s new entry-level vehicle.
Range Rover revealed the GT in July, presenting it as the fifth and newest member of the lineup. Unlike the distinct SUV design Range Rover has built the brand on, the GT is a low-slung grand tourer.
The electric GT is “a captivating new expression” of the brand, Range said, describing it as “the most technologically sophisticated” model it’s ever designed.

title: Germany's EV share hits record 37% as BEVs beat gas and diesel combined
raw_summary: Battery-electric cars took a record 37% of Germany’s new car market in October, according to data released today by the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt (KBA), the country’s federal motor vehicle authority. That’s 94,086 BEVs, up 79.5% from 52,425 a year earlier. For the second month in a row, German buyers registered more fully electric cars than gasoline and diesel cars combined. And with two months left in the year, Germany has already blown past the auto industry’s EV forecast for all of 2026.
summary: Battery-electric cars took a record 37% of Germany’s new car market in October, according to data released today by the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt (KBA), the country’s federal motor vehicle authority. That’s 94,086 BEVs, up 79.5% from 52,425 a year earlier. For the second month in a row, German buyers registered more fully electric cars than gasoline and diesel cars combined.
article_paragraphs: Battery-electric cars took a record 37% of Germany’s new car market in October, according to data released today by the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt (KBA), the country’s federal motor vehicle authority. That’s 94,086 BEVs, up 79.5% from 52,425 a year earlier.

For the second month in a row, German buyers registered more fully electric cars than gasoline and diesel cars combined. And with two months left in the year, Germany has already blown past the auto industry’s EV forecast for all of 2026.
The overall market barely grew in October. Total new car registrations rose 1.7% to 254,492 units, which means the EV growth came straight out of combustion cars.

Gasoline car registrations crashed 40.5% to 38,516 units, a 15.1% share. Diesel fell 21.6% to 23,882 units, or 9.4% of the market. Add them up and pure combustion cars made up just 24.5% of new registrations, 12.5 points less than BEVs alone.

Plug-in hybrids slipped 7.9% to 28,499 units (11.2%). So plug-ins accounted for about 48% of the German market last month, and the average CO2 emissions of new cars dropped 21.1% year-over-year to 79.4 g/km.

As we reported this summer, BEVs became the most popular powertrain in Germany for the first time in June with a 28.4% share. They’ve kept climbing every month since: 32.4% in August, 34.5% in September, and now 37% in October.

Through the first ten months of the year, Germany has registered 698,230 BEVs, up 60.7% year-over-year. That’s about 28.2% of the 2,476,290 new cars registered in 2026 so far, up from roughly 19% for the full year 2025.

And the industry didn’t see it coming. In December, the VDA, Germany’s auto industry association, forecast about 693,000 BEV registrations for all of 2026. Germany passed that in October. At the current pace, it’s on track for somewhere around 875,000 by the end of the year.

title: Waymo confirms it's shaking up its Uber relationship in January 2028
raw_summary: Waymo will end its exclusivity with Uber in the Austin and Atlanta markets starting in January 2028, co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana told Bloomberg News in a report published Wednesday. The robotaxi company will offer rides directly through its own smartphone app, like it does in other cities. article_paragraphs: Waymo will end its exclusivity with Uber in the Austin and Atlanta markets starting in January 2028, co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana told Bloomberg News in a report published Wednesday.

The robotaxi company will offer rides directly through its own smartphone app, like it does in other cities. Uber confirmed to TechCrunch Wednesday that it still plans to host Waymo robotaxis on its app for as long as the two companies agree. Waymo did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Mawakana’s comments come after reporting earlier this year by the Financial Times that Waymo was looking to get out of its deal with Uber, which was set to expire in May 2028 . Mawakana told Bloomberg that Waymo initially partnered with Uber because the ride-hail giant offered scale. But the experience for riders has been “a little bit of a crapshoot,” she said, especially because riders never know for sure if they’re going to hail a robotaxi or a human-driven car.
“It’s important for us to have that relationship with the rider. We’ve gotten that feedback from the riders in those markets,” Mawakana said.
Uber — which has many robotaxi and other autonomous vehicle partners — told Bloomberg that it was Waymo’s idea not to add an option in the ride-hail giant’s app to book a robotaxi directly.

After taking a prototype Fathom for a test drive last month, Ford CEO Jim Farley was reportedly blown away by the small truck’s handling and performance, calling it a “breakthrough product.” He also said the Fathom is on track to hit the market toward the end of 2027, though the team will need to keep developing at a rapid pace to get it out on time and within budget.

Ford announced the Fathom’s starting price in August. At $29,945, the pickup truck offers an affordable way to enter the EV world, and it’s the first to ride on Ford’s Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform. The Fathom is already confirmed to be equipped with a touchscreen, built-in Apple Maps, Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, and Blue Cruise hands-free driving capabilities.

The UEV platform operates on a 400-volt electrical architecture, so charging won’t be as quick as vehicles that use an 800-volt system, but Ford says the trade-off for a lighter, more affordable vehicle is worth it. It’ll also use a 48-volt system instead of the traditional 12-volt system used in most vehicles; the higher voltage is intended to increase power and fuel efficiency. Farley revealed this week that the platform will break up the electrical components into five distinct zones to simplify production processes and reduce costs.

The Fathom’s starting price puts it on the more affordable end of the entire car market, including gas-powered and hybrid vehicles, but higher trim levels often bring a significantly higher price to a new car. Ford, however, is reportedly aiming to keep even the highest Fathom trim below $40,000. It’s unclear what will be included in the base model versus the higher specs, but top trims will likely have a longer range, among other upgrades.

The Fathom’s pre-order list is expected to open in the first quarter of 2027, and the truck is slated to go on sale in the last quarter of the year. Pricing beyond the Fathom’s entry point hasn’t yet been announced, but it seems even the highest trim will remain relatively affordable.

If you remember, Musk has long been reported to want his companies all under one roof to complete Tesla's tranformation into an AI/robotics company (or stop making cars without crashing the stock price). xAI already merged with Twitter and stuck Musk's antisemitism-spewing, CSAM-generating chatbot in Teslas , then merged with Spacex ahead of its IPO . As previously reported, Musk had then ordered Tesla to look at spinning off its China business to help his main division merge with SpaceX more easily. Musk also floated the possibility with investors, and one of the Trump administration's lasting legacies will be its love of corporate mergers, so it sounded plausible.

With Democrats winning control of both the House and the Senate, likely finishing with 258 Representatives and 55 (or 56!) Senators, the left doesn't just have power, it has a mandate from the voters to put a stop to everything the Trump administration is doing. Raskin will chair the House Judiciary Committee, Garcia will chair the House Oversight Committee, and both have promised investigations into any criminal activity that's taken place. That's not exactly fertile ground for a major corporate merger, especially after Musk attempted to inflame a race riot in Ireland, campaigned for Germany's Nazi-adjacent AfD party, and blew hundreds of millions of dollars trying to elect Republicans.

Yes, our friends over at the Tesla Takedown kept a running thread going last night, highlighting every race Musk lost and how much money he wasted. Nearly two dozen races, all won by Dems, even though a Republican billionaire tried to buy their elections. Per Vanity Fair , Musk dumped an eye-watering $474 million into this election, and he still got kicked in the nards. He could have given $50,000 to 9,400 people and still wasted less of his money.

Democrats who haven't been bought off by the crypto and AI lobbies have been sounding the alarm in recent months about the dangers of any one person having as much power as Elon does. The man has the power to slow down Ukraine's military's internet , and the prospect of combining SpaceXAI with the most valuable car company in the world makes a lot of regulators nervous. Expect it to be a fight with the centrists in the party, but Dems are more likely to try to weaken Musk's power, not hand him a win.

Because our election system is weird, Republicans won't lose power until January and could theoretically rush the merger through. But even the Motley Fool — a website that published " Prediction: SpaceX Stock Will Go Parabolic After Nov. 6 " the day both Tesla and SpaceX shares plunged — doesn't think that's likely. In an article foolishly calling the merger "inevitable ," the MFers timeline is still "within the next 12 months" not "before January." They also admit many factors, including antitrust enforcement could be a problem for the merger.

With Dems winning a huge mandate to govern, Republican politicians should be less willing to stick their necks out for that eternally sticky loser, too, so calling it "inevitable" is certainly a take. More importantly, Republicans have a much more important activity on their agenda than facilitating this merger. With Trump humiliated and unable to run for a third term anyway, Republicans are leaderless. When they move from depression to anger, they're going to start pointing fingers. Infighting and power struggles are inevitable unless Republicans just give up completely.

With Tucker Carlson and Marjorie Taylor-Greene-whatever waiting in the wings, the far-right giving up isn't likely either. So expect Republicans to be distracted, Democrats to feel emboldened, Jeffries and Schumer to remain spineless cowards, and Elon Musk to struggle getting any attempt at a Tesla-SpaceX merger off the ground. That's probably something Elon's sad about, but for the rest of us, it can only be good news any time Elon's dreams go up in smoke.

Ferrari made the announcement that its first all-electric vehicle was sold out through '27 during its earnings call earlier this week, according to InsideEVs . The news comes after a July announcement from the automaker that the $560,800 EV had already hit its 2026 sales target after being available for purchase for just a couple of months. People want this thing, and people want pronouns in email signatures again. It's morning again in America.

"The Luce that we plan to sell next year basically are all allocated," Benedetto Vigna, Ferrari CEO, said in the earnings call, according to InsideEVs, adding that customers who placed an order now would have to wait a year to actually take delivery. Hopefully this isn't an empty promise, like "gas prices are going to come down after the midterms." Anyway, Ferrari hasn't said how many Luces it plans to sell, and it hasn't provided any sort of regional breakdown of orders so far.

Like Jon Ossoff and his lightning-fast election night, Ferrari made quick work of its 2026 sales goal. Two unnamed sources told the Financial Times that the automaker planned to sell just under 500 examples of the Jony Ive-designed EV this year, and doing it in such a quick fashion is quite the indictment on what the average internet car enthusiast thinks a popular car should be. Long term, Ferrari says it wants to sell about 2,500 Luces by 2030, or roughly 600 per year, though the exact ramp-up numbers haven't been released yet.

When the Luce first launched, you'd be hard-pressed to find a fan. Folks didn't like its looks, the fact it was a sedan, or the EV-ness of it all. People who never thought about cars were letting the takes fly , but Ferrari has remained steadfast. It has defended the Luce, attempting to showcase its new tech while also reaching the next generation of wealthy buyers in China and other tech hubs like Silicon Valley. Basically, they're targeting folks who are already driving EVs but are looking for something more premium.

Still, this hasn't stopped people, even though with close ties to Ferrari, from throwing hissy fits over the Luce. When the car first launched, we reported that Ferrari's former longtime CEO, Luca di Montezemolo , told reporters that if he were to say what he really thought about the Luce, he'd "be doing Ferrari a disservice" and it risked "destroying a legend." He even said that he hoped Ferrari would "at least remove the prancing horse from that car."
In any case, it's time to jump in the Luce, crank up "Fight Song" and blast down the highway, because we're libbing out in this bih.

Walkable communities are as old as the hills. That’s what people did before automobiles hit the scene and cities were organized around cars. Credit for applying the walkability model to 21st century urban planning goes to the Franco-Colombian scientist Carlos Moreno, who formalized the 15 Minute City concept in 2016. The idea got a further boost of attention when the Mayor of Paris, Anne Hidalgo, pitched walkable, bike-able neighborhoods as part of her successful re-election campaign in 2020.

The COVID-19 lockdown of 2020 was also a pivotal moment, with a surge in work-from-home households drawing attention to the need for local resources as a matter of survival and resiliency in case of a widespread emergency.

The 15 Minute City model covers a lot of ground, but the basic idea is that people should be able to do their shopping, recreation, socializing, and other essential routines within walking or biking distance from their homes, making cars largely optional within the neighborhood. Walkable access to schools and health care is also part of the plan.

The argument for 15-minute cities (also called 15-minute neighborhoods or 15-minute communities) is also pretty straightforward. Walking is healthier than sitting in a car. Avoiding injury or death from car accidents is another plus. Walking also reduces carbon emissions, and it saves money on gas.

In addition, walkability levels the playing field, so to speak. Everyone in the 15-minute zone has walkable access to basic resources, regardless of whether or not they can afford a car. In other words, there is a significant equity and inclusion element to the concept…

…and, that’s where the trouble kicks in. In 2022 the World Economic Forum posted an article by Lisa Chamberlain, the founder of the urban communications and business firm Strategies for City Builders. Chamberlain describes a 15 Minute City as characterized by diversified, mixed-use neighborhoods built to withstand shocks like COVID-19 and climate change.

“As climate change and global conflict cause shocks and stresses at faster intervals and increasing severity, the 15-minute city will become even more critical,” Chamberlain emphasized, with a further emphasis on equity and inclusion:

In the latest batch of new energy vehicles (NEVs) approved for sale by China’s MIIT (Ministry of Information Technology) this week, a new all-electric Denza N9 appeared.
The filing revealed the Denza N9 EV will be available with three electric motors, delivering a combined output of 1,193 horsepower (890 kW).
A badge on the back reveals it will use BYD’s tri-motor e3 platform. The setup features a single 362 horsepower (270 kW) front motor and two 415 horsepower (310 kW) rear electric motors.

The electric version measures 5,270 mm long, 2,030 mm wide, and 1,830 mm tall, with a 3,125 mm wheelbase, which is the same as the current Denza N9 PHEV Flash Charging model. It will be available in five- and six-seat configurations.
While the filing reveals it will use a lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery with cells from BYD’s battery unit, FinDreams, it does not provide specifics like capacity or driving range.

raw_title: SpaceX Starship Will Need To Re-Fuel 22 Times In Space To Make It To The Moon
title: SpaceX Starship Will Need To Re-Fuel 22 Times In Space To Make It To The Moon
raw_summary: As NASA plans to send astronauts back to the surface of the Moon in 2028 , there's still the small matter of figuring out how to get them there. While the Artemis II mission proved that we can send people around the Moon and bring them safely home, the space agency needs a way to take astronauts out of the Orion capsule and down to the actual ground. The original plan was for a SpaceX Starship to fulfill this duty, and that could still be the case. But delays in the development of that ambitious rocket caused NASA to re-open the contract, which allowed Blue Origin to toss its hat in the ring . Still, SpaceX insists it will fend off this challenge from a rival billionaire-owned space company and win the contract all over again. The only thing standing in its way: the minor fact that it has to refuel the Starship in-orbit, something never done before and that SpaceX hasn't even attempted yet. Oh, and it has to do it many, many times. How many? Great question. The NASA Aerospace Safety Advisory Panel recently announced that, by their calculations, a Starship would require fully 22 in-orbit refuelings to get that one single rocket to the Moon's surface, per Ars Technica . Again, the total number of times that any rocket has ever done this is zero. Specifically, the plan from SpaceX is to launch one Starship into orbit to act as a fuel depot; then launch many other Starships to load up that first one with fuel; then launch a final Starship to take on that fuel from the depot and head out to the Moon.

Again, the total number of times that any rocket has ever done this is zero. Specifically, the plan from SpaceX is to launch one Starship into orbit to act as a fuel depot; then launch many other Starships to load up that first one with fuel; then launch a final Starship to take on that fuel from the depot and head out to the Moon.

If 22 sounds like an insane number to you, you're not alone: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said on the social media platform X, which SpaceX owns, "Actual number will be more like 6 to 8." That makes for quite a broad range of estimates. The reason this is so fuzzy is because the fuel we're talking about here isn't gasoline, but rather a mixture of liquid oxygen and methane . This actually boils off in the vacuum of space, so how much fuel can be transferred depends on the efficiency of the technology involved. Technology that has never actually been tested in orbit.

Currently, SpaceX plans to perform its first test of orbital refueling in early 2027 , just a little over a year before it will theoretically do it for the Moon landing. If that doesn't work, well, SpaceX's lunar ambitions are in trouble. Even if it does go well, and there are absolutely no issues whatsoever with this unprecedented capability, there's still the small matter of actually launching all of these rockets. Right now, the still-in-development Starship only launches once every few months. Musk claims it will be launching weekly by early 2027, just months away. And then he further claims it will launch twice a week by the end of 2027. Let's just say that would be, ah, truly remarkable if it happened.

For once, let us be optimistic, and believe in words. If these words be true, and Starship truly is launching twice-weekly, then launching 22 refueling Starships (plus launching the initial "depot" Starship) would take... three months. And that is assuming no failures, either of the rockets or of the fuel transfer process. That's reduced to three weeks if you also believe Musk's figure of six launches. At least Musk has never once lied about his companies capabilities! If for some reason you don't believe in that launch cadence, then total refueling will take potentially years . Either way, that would amount to the most complicated endeavor NASA, or any space entity, has ever attempted.

By contrast, Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin has a much simpler plan to get to the Moon. It's still complicated, let's be clear, but less so than SpaceX. The company's proposal calls for a mere four launches of its New Glenn rocket, assuming it doesn't explode and destroy its entire launchpad, again . The first three would park a booster stage in orbit; the fourth would put a Blue Moon lunar lander into orbit, where it will collect all the booster stages, stack them together, and then blast off towards the Moon. That is a wild dance all its own, but it doesn't require figuring out how to transfer any fuel.

If you're wondering where the actual astronauts are, don't you worry: they're on a completely different rocket altogether. The Space Launch System (SLS) rocket carries the Orion capsule into orbit with all the astronauts on board. The capsule then continues on from Earth orbit to lunar orbit on its own, as the Artemis II mission demonstrated. Somewhere along that path — whether in high-Earth orbit, high-lunar orbit, or low-lunar orbit (this part still isn't nailed down) — the Orion capsule will have to dock with either the Starship or the Blue Moon, depending on who wins the contract. The lander will then land, the astronauts will enjoy a nice walk around another world, and then the lander will return to lunar orbit. Then it's back aboard the Orion capsule and then back to Earth.

Sounds easy! Basically, a lot has to go right for NASA to make that 2028 landing date. How it shakes out in practice depends on how well a lot of untested equipment and procedures work. Then again, if you were to go back to the 1960s, the Apollo program wasn't exactly any more precedented, or safer. In that decade, though, NASA did have a lot more testing demonstrations before going for the Moon. This time around, the agency wants to get there faster.
bullet_points: As NASA plans to send astronauts back to the surface of the Moon in 2028 , there's still the small matter of figuring out how to get them there.

While the Artemis II mission proved that we can send people around the Moon and bring them safely home, the space agency needs a way to take astronauts out of the Orion capsule and down to the actual ground.

raw_summary: The term "body style" is an all-encompassing label used to describe the size, shape, and characteristics of a vehicle. For example, sedans and pickup trucks are two popular vehicle body styles in the United States. At Car and Driver , we separate vehicles into eight primary body styles, making them easier to categorize (and easier for you to shop). Within those eight broad body styles are a host of different variations that get even more specific. Size is one of the most important distinctions. We typically categorize vehicles in the following sizes, listed in increasing order: subcompact, compact, mid-size, and full-size. There are also differences in luxury vehicles versus non-luxury vehicles, and some vehicles that defy categorization altogether. Not sure where the car you’re interested in fits? There are also differences in luxury vehicles versus non-luxury vehicles, and some vehicles that defy categorization altogether. Not sure where the car you’re interested in fits? We've broken down all of the main vehicle types and their subcategories to help you understand the body style basics.

Sedans are what most people picture when they think of a traditional passenger car. Sedans have four doors and incorporate a three-box design (jargon for a design with a distinct hood, passenger compartment, and trunk). Sedans come in multiple types and sizes, ranging from fuel-efficient and small compact to luxurious and large full-size options.

The smallest sedans in the U.S. are subcompact in size. Among non-luxury options, there are no sedans remaining in this segment, as automakers have dropped these entry-level options. The luxury subcompact segment is more flush with options. This subset includes the Audi A3 and Mercedes CLA-class .

Compact sedans are larger than subcompacts but smaller than mid-size models. Both mainstream and luxury options abound. In either form, compacts tend to offer reasonable space for cargo and people, though taller individuals may find these models’ rear seat room a bit too confining. The Honda Civic is a benchmark of the mainstream compact segment, as it expertly blends a reasonably roomy rear seat and trunk with enjoyable driving dynamics for a reasonable price. It’s why the model’s practically a regular on our 10Best Cars .

Mid-size sedans tend to sacrifice some of the driving enjoyment of their compact kin for additional rear seat and cargo space. These machines are perfect for those who regularly carry passengers or haul various items. The best mid-size sedans afford this extra versatility with only a marginal hit to behind-the-wheel joy. This includes the 10Best-winning Honda Accord in the mainstream segment and vehicles such as the BMW 5-series in the mid-size luxury segment.

Full-size sedans these days are the flagship models in a brand’s lineup. Only luxury-badged full-size sedans remain, as previous mainstream full-size options such as the Ford Taurus were discontinued years ago. The luxurious Mercedes-Benz S-class is a prime example of the category. Such sedans tend to emphasize a comfortable ride and loads of rear seat space above all else.

Sports sedans come in subcompact, compact, mid-size, and full-size forms. These models tend to be high-performance variants of more run-of-the-mill models, though some may argue that a number of these “run-of-the-mill” options are sports sedans in and of themselves. For instance, the subcompact Cadillac CT4 and compact Cadillac CT5 feature engaging rear-drive dynamics that arguably make these sedans worthy of the title. However, we limit the sports sedan designation to the models' truly sporty 10Best-winning CT4-V Blackwing and CT5-V Blackwing variants.

Xiaomi Tech posted the video on X on November 3, as the company picked up awards at the World Internet Conference in Wuzhen. It shows the robots pulling side covers from bins, carrying them to storage racks, and placing them into slots, with a running clock of cumulative working time and an “Autonomous, 100x Speed” label in the corner.

8 hours on the production line. 🤖 Xiaomi’s full-size humanoid robot takes on an 8-hour task at the Center Console Side-Cover Sorting Workstation at Xiaomi Auto Factory. Beyond sustained operation, it can autonomously detect and correct anomalies while coordinating with the… pic.twitter.com/brpO3S5bCn

According to Xiaomi, the robot covered the full day of production needs at that workstation. The company says it detected and corrected anomalies on its own and coordinated with the production line’s control system, calling it “another step toward real-world industrial deployment.”

This is the third milestone in a program Xiaomi has been running in public all year. In March, it put a humanoid in its Beijing EV factory as an “intern” installing self-tapping nuts. Xiaomi reported a 90.2% success rate over three hours, fast enough to meet the station’s 76-second cycle time. By July, it said that success rate was up to 98%, and it added two harder stations, including the side-cover sorting job from this week’s video.
Last December, Xiaomi’s CEO, Lei Jun, said the company plans to deploy humanoid robots in large numbers across its factories within five years.

Xiaomi also announced that its open-source Xiaomi-Robotics-1 AI model, pre-trained on 100,000 hours of real-world robot data, has started trial runs in Xiaomi staff apartments. In a 30-minute run, it completed more than 50 task chains across three rooms.

raw_title: Puerto Rico tapped Sunrun’s home batteries for 18 straight days
title: Puerto Rico tapped Sunrun's home batteries for 18 straight days
raw_summary: Sunrun has doubled participation in its Puerto Rico virtual power plant to more than 60,000 customers, and the grid is putting those home batteries to work: It tapped into them for 18 straight days in October. A virtual power plant (VPP) connects batteries across thousands of properties and coordinates them to supply power together.
summary: Sunrun has doubled participation in its Puerto Rico virtual power plant to more than 60,000 customers, and the grid is putting those home batteries to work: It tapped into them for 18 straight days in October. A virtual power plant (VPP) connects batteries across thousands of properties and coordinates them to supply power together.
article_paragraphs: Sunrun has doubled participation in its Puerto Rico virtual power plant to more than 60,000 customers, and the grid is putting those home batteries to work: It tapped into them for 18 straight days in October.
A virtual power plant (VPP) connects batteries across thousands of properties and coordinates them to supply power together.

Sunrun says its VPP network in Puerto Rico now includes nearly 70,000 batteries, frequently delivering 45 megawatts (MW) for four hours at a time. It has dispatched them more than 60 times since April, including daily deployments beginning October 13 during unusually hot weather.

For Puerto Ricans, who pay some of the highest electricity prices in the US, getting reliable power for all that money remains a problem. Residential electricity averaged 26.36 cents per kilowatt-hour in August, compared with a US average of 18.16 cents, according to the US Energy Information Administration (EIA).

That makes the batteries already installed at homes pretty useful. The grid can pay to tap their stored energy when supplies get tight, putting existing equipment to work without waiting for a new power plant to be built.
Sunrun’s network grew from around 4,000 customers in 2024 to more than 30,000 in 2025. It says it’s the largest aggregator in Puerto Rico’s Customer Battery Energy Sharing (CBES) program.

LUMA, the island’s grid operator, calls on CBES when it expects electricity demand or reserve needs to exceed available generation. Companies such as Sunrun then manage the battery response automatically.

Homeowners get paid for sharing energy and choose how much to keep for backup. Sunrun says most share a small portion of their total battery capacity; the company earns recurring revenue for operating the network.

Alpina began as a German tuner company in the early 1960s that specialized in high-performance engines with the ultimate comfortable cabin. Rather than outfitting BMWs to attack tracks, Alpina built cars that glided on pavement and wrapped drivers in luxury materials. BMW recently took control of the company and re-established it as a subbrand, much like Mercedes-Maybach .

We reported early this year that the first BMW Alpina production car would likely be inspired by the 7-series. Then, in May, the automaker unveiled the Vision BMW Alpina concept , which was said to be inspiration for the upcoming model. New photos and videos of the prototype Alpina show strong 7-series bones, with the build taking on more of a standard sedan silhouette than the concept’s smooth, sweeping rear end.

No Alpina is complete without its signature 20-spoke wheels, and BMW says the upcoming model takes the light alloy rollers to the next level by wrapping them in specially developed tires with a layer of foam inside for a smoother ride. Talk about bougie.

Tech specs are still few and far between, and the only thing BMW has confirmed in terms of performance is that the Alpina will be powered by a V-8. A video from BMW shows the car reaching over 186 mph during high-speed testing in Italy. Since this isn’t a track-focused model, the exterior lacks some of the aero bits that would normally accompany a faster, more expensive BMW. Instead, most of the Alpina’s standout exterior qualities are found in the rear, where quad-oval exhaust pipes and a small spoiler break up the standard 7-series’s body lines.

Based on the video below, the interior looks pretty similar to the 7-series, with a thin panoramic display and two screens along the dashboard. It gets the same four-spoke steering wheel as the 7-series, but the seats seem to be a bit different than the stock option, and it’s likely the cabin will be dressed in upgraded materials.

The ultra-luxury sedan will be the first to roll out under BMW Alpina, and it’s expected to arrive sometime next year. BMW hasn’t said what else is on the horizon for the brand, though it’s likely the three-row BMW X7 SUV will be the next to get Alpina treatment.

Alayna Wilkening grew up reading motorsport magazines and following her grandpa around his Chevrolet dealership's showroom floor. In true Hoosier fashion, her first car was a hot pink custom cardboard "Fiero-vette" for her kindergarten Kindy 500 race. She now autocrosses a 1994 Miata with her dad, which she learned to drive the night before her first event. Alayna went to Indiana University and graduated with a degree in journalism and a minor in graphic design. As a testament to her great taste in cars, her first real one was a metallic orange 2007 Chevy HHR, which she lovingly called "The Dumptruck."

Votes are still being tallied, but Mississippi and Alaska may well go blue too. Kansas has its first Democratic senator in nearly a century! Voters have soundly rejected Trump and the Republicans, which could spell some real complications for the party and the automakers that allied with it. From NBC :
President Donald Trump told voters to pretend he was on the ballot in this year's midterm elections.
They did. And they resoundingly rejected both his policies and his Republican Party.

Democrats have captured full control of Congress, NBC News projects, with voters delivering a forceful repudiation of Trump's agenda, coupled with a clear-cut message that Congress has not done enough to provide checks on his administration and needs to do more to address affordability and corruption.

The Trump administration of the last couple years has spent its time rolling back emissions regulations , destroying EV incentives , and generally cordoning off the U.S. automotive market as a little piece of history — somewhere automakers need not innovate to compete. With the legislative branch going blue, though, we may well see new environmental regulations. What will that mean for automakers that cozied up to the MAGA camp? Will we start to match European regulations and resume our EV push? Only time will tell, but all those automakers that returned to V8s may well regret their investments.

Elon Musk was the single largest donor in the 2026 election cycle, having spent nearly half a billion dollars backing Republican candidates across the country. Not only were his efforts for naught, but his adoptive home state of Texas has gone entirely blue — governor, senate, attorney general, even the railroad commissioner. raw_title: This V-16 Resurrects a Forgotten Engine Architecture for a Custom Build
title: This V-16 Resurrects a Forgotten Engine Architecture for a Custom Build
raw_summary: “If you have two V-8s that are exactly in the same timing, your pistons aren’t firing properly; it can rip itself apart—not good.” That’s Bryan Fuller summarizing the challenges presented by physically joining a pair of LS3 V-8 engines to create an 854 cubic-inch V-16 reported to make in the neighborhood of 1200 horsepower. But while getting 16 holes to fire in a complementary, non-destructive manner is a feat unto itself, the impetus behind the project is a one-off custom Roadster designed by Hot Wheels with direct input from the unnamed, ostensibly well-heeled client. Fuller says the design of the 19.5-foot-long custom roadster is inspired by the 1938 Cadillac V-16 Series-90, but devotees of the brand’s history will recognize the spirit of the 1937 Cadillac V16 Hartmann Cabriolet, a two-off run of vehicles crafted in Switzerland for—you guessed it—a wealthy client.
summary: “If you have two V-8s that are exactly in the same timing, your pistons aren’t firing properly; it can rip itself apart—not good.” That’s Bryan Fuller summarizing the challenges presented by physically joining a pair of LS3 V-8 engines to create an 854 cubic-inch V-16 reported to make in the neighborhood of 1200 horsepower.
article_paragraphs: “If you have two V-8s that are exactly in the same timing, your pistons aren’t firing properly; it can rip itself apart—not good.” That’s Bryan Fuller summarizing the challenges presented by physically joining a pair of LS3 V-8 engines to create an 854 cubic-inch V-16 reported to make in the neighborhood of 1200 horsepower.

But while getting 16 holes to fire in a complementary, non-destructive manner is a feat unto itself, the impetus behind the project is a one-off custom Roadster designed by Hot Wheels with direct input from the unnamed, ostensibly well-heeled client. Fuller says the design of the 19.5-foot-long custom roadster is inspired by the 1938 Cadillac V-16 Series-90, but devotees of the brand’s history will recognize the spirit of the 1937 Cadillac V16 Hartmann Cabriolet, a two-off run of vehicles crafted in Switzerland for—you guessed it—a wealthy client.

Back in the 21st century, Fuller had to address the timing, cooling, fuel, and air issues, as well as engineer their structural unity and their combined output to ensure the V-8s play nicely together.

As for ignition timing, the rear engine is clocked back “about 45 degrees,” which allows the tandem V-8s to fire in the proper order of a V-16. A single starter spins both. The mating of the torque is achieved by mounting a giubo joint (a.k.a. flex disc), a flex joint comprised of a rubber or urethane center with metal mounting plates on either side that mates the rear of the front engine with the front of the rear engine. Structural connection of the V-8s is made via a trio of CNC-machined plates, one in the center valley and one each on the lower right and left sides.

Ignition is handled traditionally, with two computers and individual plug wires, Fuller noted that “the LS3 is a known quantity,” and years of tuning the LS3 V-8 makes the job a little easier. Cooling is the only shared major system. A Meziere water pump generates enough pressure to move the coolant through both engines, out a custom dual outlet, and into a single radiator. Air is handled by a highly modified Holley intake that will continue to be modified as the project moves to installing the powertrain in the body.

The Tremec T-56 Magnum transmission was optimized by Bowler Performance Transmissions, who polished the internals, among other tweaks. As expected, ARP hardware is utilized throughout the project. Even the powertrain table it sits on is custom-built.

At this point, the V-16 is waiting for the Roadster Shop to finish the custom chassis so the team can begin the process of combining all three elements to create a fully operational vehicle. How long that process will take is unclear, but the V-16 makes a pretty nice conversation piece just as it sits on its custom display stand.

A Rust Belt native and tireless supporter of the region, he grew up immersed in automotive, marine, and aviation culture. A lifetime of hands-on experience and a healthy dose of skepticism provide him the tools to deliver honest and informative news, reviews, and editorial perspective. To assess Rivian’s latest effort, we lined up a 2027 Rivian R2 Performance against a Tesla Model Y Performance in a battle of high-tech, superquick electric SUVs.
See all results for new 2027 Rivian R2 for sale near 20147

While Rivian plans to sell a $46,485 base model starting next year, the R2 launched for the 2027 model year exclusively in the punchy Performance trim. Initial versions come standard with the Launch package, which includes the hands-free driving assistance system and a 4400-pound tow package, which on later R2s will cost $2500 and $950, respectively. The example we drove had the standard setup of all-season tires wrapped around 21-inch wheels, with the only option, $2000 Launch Green paint, bringing the total to $61,485. The boxy newcomer faces off against an EV mainstay in the Model Y. The Performance model we tested had but one option, Full Self-Driving (Supervised), so we tacked on three years’ worth of the $99-per-month subscription, $3564, to come in at $63,194. Tesla fits the Model Y Performance with a trailer hitch as standard, and the sporty SUV can tow up to 3500 pounds.

The R2 and Model Y may be direct competitors, but they take on drastically different shapes. The Model Y features Tesla’s signature egg-like silhouette, and while lesser Model Ys are fairly anonymous looking, the Performance looks pretty sharp in Ultra Red paint with black wheels and trim. The Performance also sports a reshaped front bumper and a small rear lip spoiler.

The R2 is more rectangular, essentially looking like a shrunken version of the R1S. Rivian’s ovoid headlights are more distinctive and affable than the Tesla’s front light bar, which has the menacing look of the eyes on Iron Man’s mask. The R2’s front bumper, with an integrated silver skid plate and tow hooks, hints at the Rivian’s more outdoorsy aura.

The different vibes continue inside, despite both automakers heavily favoring screens over physical controls. In typical Tesla fashion, the Model Y’s interior feels bare, centered around the 16-inch touchscreen. The dashboard, door panels, and center console all have a simple, bland design, although ambient lighting injects a bit of pizzazz. The Performance model’s front seats get more substantial bolstering and a fun “warp speed” badge nestled in below the headrest. Build quality and materials quality have improved greatly since the Model Y’s early days, and carbon-fiber inserts imbue the Performance with a sporty feel. But the materials still aren’t as rich as those in the Rivian—Tesla’s vegan faux leather feels slightly plasticky, and the soft-touch surfaces aren’t as plush.

article_paragraphs: Fresh doubts have emerged over the future of Cadillac Formula 1's majority ownership amid reports Mark Walter's TWG Global is looking to offload some of its shares - with Liverpool FC owner Fenway Sports Group said to be among the interested parties.

US billionaire Walter and his companies are the subject of a federal probe by the U.S. Department of Justice, investigating whether Walter's insurance companies, including Delaware Life Insurance Company, Clear Spring Life and Annuity, improperly invested policyholder funds in affiliated businesses. The transactions reportedly involved are around $20 billion in loans and investments that allegedly were not adequately disclosed.

Some of those funds were allegedly used to expand Walter's burgeoning sports empire, which at one point included the LA Dodgers baseball team, LA Lakers basketball team, a minority stake in football club Chelsea, and the LA Sparks WNBA team. TWG Global has consistently denied any wrongdoing.

TWG Global is also the parent company of TWG Motorsports, which majority owns the Cadillac F1 team as well as its NASCAR, IndyCar, IMSA and Australian Supercars squads. The Cadillac brand's parent company General Motors also holds an undisclosed minority share in the F1 team as it supplies infrastructure and personnel, and is developing future power units.

Walters has already moved to sell the Lakers and his 12.8% share in Chelsea, and the LA Sparks are also up for sale. Sports business website Sportico has now reported that Walter is also looking to offload part of his majority stake in the Cadillac F1 team, valuing the team at around $3billion.

The Washington Post has reported that one of several interested parties is John Henry's Fenway Sports Group, which owns Liverpool FC and the Boston Red Sox baseball team. FSG recently sold 38% of its stake in Liverpool, and already has a presence in motorsports as a 50% shareholder of the RFK Racing team in NASCAR.

While TWG Global initially dismissed suggestions it could sell part of its F1 team, there are plausible reasons why it could be the next asset up for sale if Walter is forced to replace the related-party loans in question with fresh capital.
Walter’s group, Guggenheim Baseball Partners, purchased the LA Dodgers for $2.15 billion in 2012 out of bankruptcy court.

For EICMA , the company revealed a new generation for the Africa Twin line, bumping the bike from CRF1100L to CRF1150L with tech, styling, and comfort updates to match. The biggest change, though, is a new third sibling in the AT line: Africa Twin and Africa Twin Adventure Sports, meet the Africa Twin Enduro Sports. Honda claims 117 horsepower and 88 pounds-feet of torque from the new mill, though those are global numbers. It's a trick that worked on my old F800GS, and it'll likely make the new Africa Twin feel smaller than its as-yet-unannounced weight.

For EICMA , the company revealed a new generation for the Africa Twin line, bumping the bike from CRF1100L to CRF1150L with tech, styling, and comfort updates to match. The biggest change, though, is a new third sibling in the AT line: Africa Twin and Africa Twin Adventure Sports, meet the Africa Twin Enduro Sports.

The new engine is a 1,131 cc parallel twin, presumably with the same 270-degree crank offset that's so in vogue right now. Honda claims 117 horsepower and 88 pounds-feet of torque from the new mill, though those are global numbers. If they're from the European-spec bike, expect some differences for our U.S. emissions and noise regulations. That engine's bolted to a new frame, one that tucks the fuel tank beneath the seat to lower the center of gravity. It's a trick that worked on my old F800GS, and it'll likely make the new Africa Twin feel smaller than its as-yet-unannounced weight.

The big news out of the Africa Twin line is the new variant, the Africa Twin Enduro Sports. Honda is pitching this as a bigger brother to the CRF450, to which the company says the ES has "front suspension ... specifications" that are "equivalent." It's anyone's guess as to what that actually means on two bikes with different frames, dimensions, and riding styles, but Honda is certainly making it clear that the Enduro Sports is meant to be the most focused off-road member of the Africa Twin family — at least, as focused as any adventure bike can get.

It's always been a bit comical to see people lugging farkled-out GSes through BDRs that would better suit a DR650, but now it seems Honda has made an Africa Twin for people who want to rip through dunes. Is a 500-plus-pound ADV the way to do that? No. Maybe the bike is targeted at Pol Tarres specifically.

While the Enduro Sports is a whole new variant in the lineup, Honda hasn't forgotten the standard AT and the AS. Both get what Honda is very concisely calling "Showa Electronically Equipped Ride Adjustment electronically controlled suspension with Honda Skyhook control," which I will simply be calling "Skyhook" from here on out because, Jesus Christ. Honda claims its Skyhook will adapt damping in near real time to insulate the rider from the texture of the road surface, a touring comfort feature that points toward these two models being more road-oriented than prior Africa Twins — even if the base bike keeps its 21-inch front wheel.

That electronic suspension is paired with the usual bevy of electronic rider aids: Lean-sensitive ABS, traction control, and stability control, all of which can be changed for six different rider modes. Honda of course also offers its dual-clutch transmission, long a staple of the Africa Twin lineup, likely across all three variants.

As usual, the Adventure Sports model remains the most road-touring oriented, with a larger 6.34-fuel tank (Honda didn't say the capacity of the tank on the base and ES models) and a unique fairing design. It retains the 19-inch front wheel of the outgoing model, cross-spoked for tubeless compatibility, and Honda has now given the bike some Gold Wing-tier software: Honda Sensing Ride, a system available on DCT bikes that uses dual front and rear radar units to monitor the area around the bike.

The front radar enables adaptive cruise control, but Honda went one step further and gave its adaptive cruise the ability to come to a complete stop in traffic and resume moving when the car ahead of you does — a system I'm not sure I want on a bike. The radar also enables forward and rear collision warnings, brake assist, and a group ride mode for staggered riding.

By Tesla’s own numbers, that covers 99% of the Teslas it sold in Korea last year. Citizens United for Consumer Sovereignty plans to file the complaint with the Korea Fair Trade Commission (KFTC) on Thursday, according to Reuters, which reviewed it.
article_paragraphs: A South Korean consumer group is asking regulators to stop Tesla from marketing “Full Self-Driving” to customers whose cars can’t legally run it. By Tesla’s own numbers, that covers 99% of the Teslas it sold in Korea last year.

Citizens United for Consumer Sovereignty plans to file the complaint with the Korea Fair Trade Commission (KFTC) on Thursday, according to Reuters, which reviewed it. It comes just a week after a Seoul court threw out a refund lawsuit from Korean owners who paid for FSD.

It all comes down to where the car was built. The Model S, Model X, and Cybertruck come from US factories and enter Korea under the KORUS free trade agreement, which recognizes US safety standards. Those are the only Teslas that got “FSD (Supervised)” when Tesla switched it on in Korea late last year.
The problem is that those don’t represent the vast majority of Tesla vehicles sold in Korea.
The Model 3 and Model Y sold in Korea come from Giga Shanghai. There’s no equivalent deal with China, so those cars need Korean approval that FSD doesn’t have.

And that’s most of the fleet. Tesla Korea country manager Seo Young-deuk told lawmakers last month that FSD works on about 20% of Teslas registered in the country. Tesla has sold more than 170,000 Shanghai-built vehicles in Korea since 2023, per data it handed to the National Assembly, and sales of those China-made cars grew more than fivefold between 2023 and 2025.

Seo’s figure also clears up the conflicting eligibility numbers we flagged when Korean police booked 80 Tesla drivers for using illegal FSD unlock devices last month. A lawmaker’s data from May put it at 2.4%, while a data firm counted 20.7% in August. Tesla’s own testimony matches the higher one.
For years, Tesla charged Korean buyers a one-time 9.043 million won (about $6,726) for FSD. It moved to a 150,000 won ($112) monthly subscription in August.

raw_title: What Risky Car Purchase Ended Up More Reliable Than People Usually Assume?
title: What Risky Car Purchase Ended Up More Reliable Than People Usually Assume?
raw_summary: A long time ago, one of my exes left town for the weekend, and I decided to entertain myself that Saturday with a visit to the nearby motorcycle dealer. I'd been slowly saving up for a bike and just wanted to take a look. Except I didn't just look. They had a bright red 2006 Ducati Monster 620 in the showroom with a price tag on it that read "$2,500." If I'd waited only a few minutes, I would have lost the bike to another customer, but I pulled the trigger just in time and became a Ducati owner. It wasn't just a Ducati Monster. The '06 models still had the old, round headlight, and the previous owner had put an Arrow carbon fiber dual exhaust on there before selling it. With the meticulous nature with which the cables were all zip-tied, and as clean as it looked, I could tell the previous owner had cared about their bike a lot. They must have loved it, too, because they clearly rode it all the time. The $2,500 Ducati that I bought on a whim became mine with 22,500 miles on the odometer didn't end up as a total disaster.

With the meticulous nature with which the cables were all zip-tied, and as clean as it looked, I could tell the previous owner had cared about their bike a lot. They must have loved it, too, because they clearly rode it all the time. The $2,500 Ducati that I bought on a whim became mine with 22,500 miles on the odometer didn't end up as a total disaster.

I rode that Monster all over Long Beach, and then when we moved to Koreatown, I rode it all over Los Angeles, too. I loved that thing so much. Until I got the keys to my Husqvarna , it was the prettiest, most special thing I'd ever owned. The ex didn't love it, but that's what breakups are for. Just kidding, we broke up for other reasons, but I won't pretend my vehicle choices haven't expanded since leaving that relationship. But despite what people usually assume , the red Italian motorcycle that's got a reputation for pricey ownership wasn't an expensive bike to own, and I'd even go as far as to call it dirt cheap.

I can't be the only person who's bought a good, dependable vehicle that other people assume is an expensive, unreliable nightmare , though. I bet plenty of you have owned a few cars that, like my Monster, are reliable in real life, even if normal people assume otherwise. And hopefully, more than a few of you have owned some cars that were somehow, magically the one reliable one that particular company built among a sea of dumpster fires. Whatever it is, head down to the comments to tell us more about the car you bought that ended up being much more reliable than other people expect.

article_paragraphs: Colton Herta may be the most high-profile name in the race to take away Valtteri Bottas's 2027 Cadillac seat, but there's an under-the-radar figure in Mercedes' return to the top of Formula 1 who is making a good case for himself too.

In the same Mexico FP1 session where Herta ticked off another superlicence point in his bid to finally get on the F1 grid (but not, as it turned out, his last), Fred Vesti was arguably the standout rookie as, in place of George Russell, he compared well to Kimi Antonelli - lapping just 0.111s slower than F1's new world champion.
Deputy Mercedes team principal Bradley Lord called it the "most impressive" of Vesti's seven F1 practice outings so far.
Vesti, who is a contender alongside the likes of Bottas, Herta and Yuki Tsunoda to be Sergio Perez's 2027 team-mate at Cadillac, openly declared after his FP1 outing: "The timing couldn't be better.

"There are discussions about a seat and I've got my eyes on that [Cadillac] seat. I believe I would be very, very good in that car and to be in Formula 1 has been my goal ever since I started driving."
The Race sat down with Vesti in Mexico to find out more about his pitch, what he thinks he could offer Cadillac, and how he's been leading the development of Mercedes' 2026 car in the virtual world.
Vesti is right that his third Mexico FP1 outing was well-timed given Cadillac is yet to make a final 2027 driver decision.

Mercedes - with the blessing of Russell - allowed Vesti to properly push on his soft tyres to show his performance potential, given some of his previous outings have been more focused on development work.

The SUV also introduces 800-volt electrical architecture, supporting DC fast charging at up to 330 kW. Under optimal conditions, Mercedes says it can add up to 303 km of range in 10 minutes. Achieving that figure will depend on charger capability, battery temperature and state of charge.

The Electric GLC brings a substantial technology upgrade, led by a 39.1-inch MBUX Hyperscreen. It runs the Mercedes-Benz Operating System, or MB.OS, supporting connected functions, intelligent navigation, driver assistance, over-the-air updates and personalised user experiences.

Exterior highlights include an illuminated grille incorporating 942 pixels. Inside, the SKY CONTROL panoramic roof with illuminated stars adds another distinctive feature to the cabin. Mercedes also highlights the use of recycled materials and materials with a reduced carbon footprint as part of the SUV’s development.

At Chakan, the Electric GLC is assembled on the same flexible line as Mercedes-Benz’s combustion-engine models. This allows the facility to handle multiple vehicle platforms and both electric and combustion powertrains under one roof.

Mercedes-Benz India has committed an additional Rs 200 crore in 2026 towards manufacturing operations, new-model preparation and digitisation. This takes its cumulative investment in India to Rs 3,200 crore.

The company says the facility runs more than 15 live AI projects, supporting quality monitoring, operational efficiency, supply-chain planning and workforce development. Camera-based inspection systems are among the tools used to monitor quality.

article_paragraphs: After a historic election defeat in one of the most expensive elections in US election history, the state of Texas has turned blue. Along with this come potential implications for Elon Musk and his companies.

The US midterm election was yesterday, and ended up in a stunning result, with Democrats taking control of both houses of Congress by wide margins, and flipping seats that had been considered safe around the nation.

Perhaps most notably, many of these seats were in Texas – a republican stronghold which saw a clean sweep, with the Democrats winning every statewide contest. Republicans maintained some state legislative power and won the State Senate, but as of this writing Democrats are currently ahead in the count for the State House.

The highest profile contest was for Texas Senate, where James Talarico won by a 55-43 margin. This race set the record for the most expensive Senate race in the nation’s history, with over half a billion dollars spent on this one seat alone.

About half of the total money spent on the race came courtesy of republican PACs, a method by which companies and the ultra-wealthy can launder money into bribes to buy elections. And most of the PAC money in the race came from one man, Elon Musk, who spent $212 million to support the enormously unpopular and scandal-ridden outgoing Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton
That’s nearly half of the $474 million dollars that Musk put into this election cycle, suggesting that he saw this race of particular importance. And yet, his candidate lost miserably.

But the rout did not stop with Paxton. Paxton’s old job as AG is now going to be filled by Democrat Nathan Johnson. And Greg Abbott, the outgoing Governor, was defeated by Gina Hinojosa. Even the less high-profile races for court seats were swept by Democrats – three seats on the 15th Court of Appeals and four seats on the Texas Supreme Court.
And those results, even beyond the big-spending Senate race, could all matter quite a lot to Elon Musk.

title: At $18,000, Could This 1997 Bentley Brooklands Let You See How The Other Half Lives?
raw_summary: Based on today's Nice Price or No Dice Bentley's price, you don't have to be a one-percent-er to live life large. Let's see if this stately and imposing saloon makes us want to live it up. On their third album, "Learning to Crawl," Chrissie Hynde and The Pretenders warned us of "Time the Avenger." A song about bad decisions, regret, and the inability to turn back the clock, it fit the album's tone perfectly, following the untimely deaths of two band members.

article_paragraphs: Based on today's Nice Price or No Dice Bentley's price, you don't have to be a one-percent-er to live life large. Let's see if this stately and imposing saloon makes us want to live it up.

On their third album, "Learning to Crawl," Chrissie Hynde and The Pretenders warned us of "Time the Avenger." A song about bad decisions, regret, and the inability to turn back the clock, it fit the album's tone perfectly, following the untimely deaths of two band members.

The fact is, time keeps marching forward, and we can never slow its pace or fully reverse its effects. That makes looking at cars like the 2001 Audi A4 Quattro Avant we considered yesterday such a scary proposition. While the seller promised that many of the car's wear-and-tear items had been addressed, with any old Audi, there's always some new surprise to darken a day and lighten a wallet. That expectation of future failures on this 25-year-old Audi gave pause, calling into question its $7,450 asking price. In the end, that was just too much to risk, and we saw an overwhelming 73% 'No Dice' loss as a result.

Okay, if you all had a hard time justifying the potential future costs of an old mid-level Audi, let's see how you do with today's far fancier-pantsed 1997 Bentley Brooklands saloon . Bentley offered the Brooklands for a short five years, from 1993 to 1998, though the model was merely an evolution of the earlier Mulsanne, introduced all the way back in 1980. That makes the model a grand dame of British luxury comportment.

Following the marque's fancy of naming its models after race tracks or sections thereof, the Brooklands takes its name from the Brooklands circuit outside of Surrey, England. It was the world's first banked oval raceway, inspiring the Indianapolis Motor Speedway when it opened in 1907 and hosting its last race in 1939. In the years in between, Bentleys raced on the track, reinforcing the model's legacy. In another unique connection, the British aircraft manufacturer Vickers located a factory at the Brooklands Aerodrome, right next to the track, and later, when this Brooklands was built, that company was the majority owner of Rolls-Royce and Bentley.

With that bit of history out of the way, let's get to just what this car is. When it was built, Bentley and Rolls-Royce were kissing cousins (I know, eww, that phrase), with both marques sharing production in Crewe on the same platform. That means that, save for its rounded grille, some suspension tuning, and a whole herd of Flying B badges, this model is essentially the same as the contemporary Rolls-Royce Silver Spirit. That means it also shares the Rolls-Royce 6.75-liter OHV V8 engine.

When it debuted in 1993, the Brooklands was meant to be a less expensive (but still very expensive) model slotted under the Turbo R. As such, it was initially available only with a naturally aspirated version of that Rolls engine. That changed in 1996, when the Brooklands got a light-pressure turbo edition, producing 300 horsepower and an impressive 442 pound-feet of torque. That's a good thing, considering this luxury barge is fitted with every comfort and convenience feature the late '90s could offer, bringing the car's weight to over 5,300 pounds. That means reasonable performance and jaw-dropping thirst for premium fuel.

This Brooklands, which the ad claims to be painted in Black Emerald Mica over a parchment Connolly leather interior with spruce trim on the dash and doors, looks to be in fabulous condition. The paint, which appears dark green in the pictures, is accented by elegant but not overwhelming chrome trim and a handsome set of factory alloy wheels.

The Brembo Group supplies all 11 teams with brake calipers in 2026, while also providing complete braking systems to selected teams.

That's been built up over 50 years in the championship and has included forming close relationships with some of F1's best ever drivers including Ayrton Senna and Michael Schumacher. In fact, a Brembo caliper philosophy favoured by Schumacher has made a comeback in 2026.
"I think mainly for the product that we do, because we are in the top-level championships, F1, MotoGP," Brembo's F1 engineer Andrea Dellavedova told The Race.

"The product itself is a very good product. All the calipers, the discs, pads, master cylinder, we are now also doing brake-by-wire. They are very good products, they are reliable and very high performance.

"The second topic is that the kind of assistance that we provide to our customers is very high, because we don't design and make the caliper, for example, sell it and then that's it. We continuously ask for feedback from the customer. We continuously try to develop the product in the way that the customer wants.
“Our job and our work is tailored to each customer. So we are very interested in the customer's opinion and needs.
“So we try to move all our design and work in general to make them happy.”

title: Ocon's F1 story is one of success, even if this is the end
raw_summary: There's really not much reason to think otherwise: it looks increasingly likely that this could be the end of Esteban Ocon's active Formula 1 career. A career blessed with plenty of highlights, a handful of podiums and a victory scored behind the wheel of a car that wasn't capable of winning on merit. He made a lot of the opportunities that came his way - not just on the track, but throughout his career. And even if it ends now, that career has already become far more than anyone could reasonably have expected, given where he started.

A career blessed with plenty of highlights, a handful of podiums and a victory scored behind the wheel of a car that wasn't capable of winning on merit.
article_paragraphs: There's really not much reason to think otherwise: it looks increasingly likely that this could be the end of Esteban Ocon's active Formula 1 career. A career blessed with plenty of highlights, a handful of podiums and a victory scored behind the wheel of a car that wasn't capable of winning on merit.

He made a lot of the opportunities that came his way - not just on the track, but throughout his career. And even if it ends now, that career has already become far more than anyone could reasonably have expected, given where he started.

There aren't many stories like his in modern F1, with kids from modest backgrounds - without wealthy families or rich sponsors behind them from an early age - reaching the pinnacle of motorsport, let alone achieving what Ocon has managed.

But his abrupt departure from Haas could well mark the end of that chapter of his racing career. Things could change. He could still return, because he's still one of the best drivers in the world. It's just very difficult to see how right now.

It's almost impossible to imagine Ocon on the grid when the 2027 season begins in Bahrain - if it begins in Bahrain - with most seats already taken and those potentially still available having plenty of candidates queuing up for them. And there's little reason to believe he'd suddenly jump ahead of the others.

There's still a question mark over Cadillac's second seat. But there's Colton Herta, with his American passport, and Yuki Tsunoda as another possible option. Liam Lawson's future hasn't been confirmed either, but Red Bull isn't suddenly going to add a 30-year-old Frenchman to the pool of candidates for its junior team. That's essentially a fight between Lawson and 19-year-old Bulgarian Nikola Tsolov.
What's more likely is that Ocon would once again have to find a place on the substitutes' bench, waiting for an opportunity until somebody slips in the shower.

And there are plenty of examples of drivers who have eventually made it back after choosing that route. Even on the current grid, Alex Albon , Valtteri Bottas and Nico Hulkenberg are examples. Ocon himself belongs in that group: he returned to racing with Renault in 2020 after spending a year on the sidelines as Mercedes' reserve driver.
